roi.payback_range: A RANGE, computed in code, never narrated here. The study prints the band running from the conservative payback month to the most likely payback month as produced by scripts/roi_math.py from the drivers above, and it never prints a single hero month. Three riders travel with the band and all three ship. ONE, the conservative end is the one to plan against, and it is the only end that carries no resold seat, no decision-data value and no qualitative benefit. TWO, the arithmetic spreads a season's benefit evenly across twelve months while the railway operates roughly five months a year (c16), so a printed month is a smoothed figure and the benefit really arrives in a burst each season. THREE, the whole band collapses if the season contact count lands under the breakeven probe volume, in which case there is no payback inside the five-season horizon, the honest answer is that this does not pay on labour, and phase two does not get funded. Any payback shorter than six months would imply unusually high volume or a tiny scope, and if the printed conservative figure comes in that fast the right response is to distrust the volume assumption rather than celebrate it.
roi.base_rate_note: THE OUTSIDE VIEW, stated before the inside view and with a wrinkle that cuts against our own pitch. THE BASE RATE IS BAD. MIT's work puts roughly 95 percent of AI pilots at no measurable P&L impact and RAND puts around 80 percent of AI projects as failures, and reference-class forecasting says the correct starting assumption for a proposal like this one is that it joins them. In this specific industry the local reference class is thin as well, only 12 percent of tour, activity and attraction operators actively use AI in their operations, with most still experimenting or not using it at all, from Arival's survey of more than 7,000 operators published October 22, 2024 (c42). Thin adoption means there is no local proof this works and no local proof it does not, which is an argument for buying measurement before buying a model, not an argument that everyone else is behind. THE HONEST WRINKLE, AND IT CHANGES HOW THE BASE RATE APPLIES RATHER THAN EXEMPTING US FROM IT. Phase one contains no artificial intelligence at all. It is a form, a server-written timestamp, an inbox ingest, a phone greeting and a governed content file. The failure modes that generate the MIT and RAND numbers are mostly model-shaped, no evaluation set, no clean data, hallucination on a liability surface, inference cost, an integration nobody assessed, drift after launch, and almost none of them can reach a system with no model in it. What phase one keeps from that base rate is the part that has nothing to do with AI, adoption. A tool the desk works around is dead whether or not it has a model, and that is the risk this build actually carries. WHERE THE AI BASE RATE DOES APPLY IS PHASE TWO, the single-node classifier on inbound free text, and phase two is not funded by this ask. It is gated on counters phase one produces, on an evaluation set built from real 2026 traffic, and on an acceptance bar set before the model is built, which is the specific discipline the failed 95 percent skip. WHY THIS ONE IS DESIGNED TO BE IN THE SMALL SHARE THAT PAYS. It is workflow-embedded rather than bolted beside the workflow, the queue is the same work the reservation agent does today with an arrival time attached (c30). It is adoption-owned by a named person on their side. It is measured, and the measurement instrument is the deliverable rather than a promise about one. Its floor is strictly above the status quo, because the timestamp is a server write and a total failure of anything downstream degrades to today's behaviour plus a timestamp. AND THE PART A VENDOR WOULD NOT SAY, we are recommending they buy an off-the-shelf tourism chat widget at published list pricing of $95 to $295 a month (c48) that we are not paid for, with the warning that under c44 the liability for what it says stays with them. Reference-class evidence we are using is labelled by tier and never used as this company's baseline, the Black Cat Cruises figures are vendor published with 10 hours a month the trustworthy number, the modelled $3,750 never quotable as revenue, and only 10 percent of site visitors leaving an email address, which cuts against capture optimism (c47). Amtrak's ARROW at 3 to 5 percent is a real precedent for a different problem (c43). Chipotle's 12 days to four and 30 percent of scheduling after hours were reported by Fortune in its own voice, and Chipotle is enormous, so the direction transfers and the magnitude does not (c46). None of those is this company's baseline and none is used as one.

Approval sits with BOB BERTO, PRESIDENT, who is also named as a director of the majority partner, so the operating decision and the ownership vote sit with the same person and this does not have to travel to an absentee owner. One item is confirmed with the company before anything ships rather than assumed, about 40 workers voted to join SMART-TD's local chapter on April 8 (c33), Reservation Agents are not among the roles that article names, and absence from a list is not proof of non-representation. THE VARIANCE CHECK, and it has an unusual shape here because there is no baseline to vary against yet. Two weeks before go-live, the desk logs contacts by channel and by hour from its own phone log and inbox, which produces the pre-baseline the whole case is missing. The first 30 days after go-live produce the measured baseline from the counters themselves. Actual versus baseline is then read at 60 days, at 90 days and at season close on the four drivers that move the answer, contacts a season, average handling minutes a contact, deflection rate on published-policy questions, and escalations a season. Every one of those is compared against the driver table in this study, line by line, and the variance is published to Nannini, Moy and Berto whether it is good or bad. Two rules ride with it. The 2026 reading is a shoulder-season sample and is labelled one, because Bennett closes September 12 (c17) and the Summit season carries no service on several late dates (c16), so a September count understates a July peak and may not be annualised without saying so. And if the measured contact count lands under the breakeven probe volume, the correct outcome is that phase two is not funded and this pilot did its job by saying no.

Average agent hours per contact today, end to end including the round trip to establish intent, booking reference and departure, assumed at 0.30 conservative, 0.35 most likely, 0.35 aggressive. No handling-time baseline exists.

Fully loaded hourly cost of a seasonal reservation agent, assumed at $32 conservative, $36 most likely, $40 aggressive, covering wage, payroll load and seasonal accommodation. No wage figure is published by the company and this is a modelled range, not a measurement.

Realisable share of handling time removed by structured intake, assumed at 18 percent conservative, 25 percent most likely, 30 percent aggressive. This is the realisable share and not the theoretical one, it is already net of the avoid-backfill test.
Realisable share of repeat policy questions deflected by the governed policy source, assumed at 30 percent conservative, 40 percent most likely, 45 percent aggressive.

Escalations and card disputes per season arising from an unreachable office inside the 24 hour clock, assumed at 40 conservative, 70 most likely, 100 aggressive, at a blended $220, $260 and $300 each, reduced 30, 40 and 45 percent. No dispute count is published, no goodwill-refund figure is published, and zero verbatim customer reviews were obtainable because every review platform returned HTTP 403, so we hold no sample of how these guests behave when this happens to them.

Capacity converts to cash on an AVOID-BACKFILL test and on no other test. The desk is seasonally staffed against a published May 1 to September 30 recruiting season (c35) with Reservation Agent openings listed for 2026 (c32), so hours removed can be realised as a seasonal shift not covered, without a layoff and without touching the represented onboard workforce (c33). No defer-hire and no redeploy dollars are claimed anywhere.

The two labour lines are asserted to be disjoint mechanisms, one shortening a handled contact and the other removing a contact from the queue. If a reader disagrees, zeroing the second line is the correct test and the conservative case should be re-read with it at zero.

Implementation assumed at $21,000 conservative, $19,000 most likely, $18,000 aggressive. Training and change management assumed at $3,000, $2,500 and $2,200, covering 16 hours of their staff time in year one and 4 hours per season after, with our materials and facilitation.

Run cost per season assumed at $3,000 conservative, $2,600 most likely, $2,400 aggressive, over 4.5 years. It carries no inference cost, no token cost and no model refresh, because phase one carries no model. Human review is not added as a run cost because the queue is worked by the agent who handles these contacts today, and that labour is netted inside the benefit lines rather than counted twice.
Contingency assumed at 20 percent conservative and most likely, 15 percent aggressive, inside the 15 to 20 band.

Year-one ramp assumed at 25 percent conservative, 30 percent most likely, 40 percent aggressive. The 2026 season closes October 7 (c16) and today is August 9, and build, inbox access and telephony configuration all come out of the same eight weeks, so the year-one ramp here is thinner than a standard ninety-day ramp rather than fatter.

Any 2026 measurement is a shoulder-season sample. Bennett closes September 12 (c17) and the Summit season carries no service on September 26 to 27 and October 1 and 3 to 5 (c16), so a question mix or contact count captured this season describes a shoulder period and may not be annualised without that label attached.

NOT ASSUMED ANYWHERE IN THIS CASE, a resold seat. Today a guest who can't reach anyone inside 24 hours forfeits all rights to a refund and the railway keeps the fare (c12), and a build that lets that guest cancel at 9pm Saturday converts a forfeiture into a refund minus a $10.00 per person penalty. Whether the resale plus the avoided dispute beats the kept fare depends on their sell-out rate by departure, the trains usually sell out in advance (c14) and no rate is published, so easier cancellation is not unambiguously positive in the short run and this case claims neither direction.

NOT ASSUMED ANYWHERE, any benefit from booking validation, booking lookup, a seat release or anything that writes to the ticketing system. That integration is out of phase one and can't be assessed from outside the company, and the booking reference is captured as an unvalidated string.

The observation that the ticketing system returned an unavailable message on 2026-08-09 (c19) is point-in-time, could be transient, is never presented as a standing condition, and carries no weight in any driver in this case.

The absence of a published IT lead on the company directory is an unverified inference about the directory and never a fact about the company. It shapes delivery toward a managed, low-maintenance build and is not used as a benefit driver.
